the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: The first commutative diagram, whose squares are cartesian because the two maps t composed with pr_i from R times_U R to U are equal, is combined with the properties of diagram (equation-pull) to produce a second commutative diagram with cartesian squares relating pr_01 and pr_02 to c composed with (i, 1) and relating pr_1 and h to s. Assume s, t have R and g has Q. Then h has Q, being the composition of s, which has R hence Q, with a base change of g, which has Q; hence the largest open W(P, h) exists. By assumption (4) applied to the base change along the R-morphisms c composed with (i, 1) over s and t, the inverse images pr_01^{-1}(W(P, h)) and pr_02^{-1}(W(P, h)) agree, both being the largest open on which c composed with (i, 1) has P. The projection U' times_{g,U,t} R to U' has a section sigma sending u' to (u', e(g(u'))), and via the displayed identification of the fibre product over U' with U' times_{g,U,t} R times_{t,U,t} R the two projections agree with pr_01 and pr_02. The equality of the two inverse images therefore exhibits W(P, h) as the inverse image of a subset, necessarily the open W = sigma^{-1}(W(P, h)), which is the desired open subscheme of U'.
